newsitem.title: UAE: Integrators seen leading in shipper satisfaction.
newsitem.headline: Integrators seen leading in shipper satisfaction.

text.p: The traditional freight industry is failing to meet shippers' demands and integrators are taking the lead in customer satisfaction, the managing director of Unisys' freight programme said on Monday.
"The cargo industry doesn't have a good history of listening to the shipper," Hugh Doyle told an air cargo conference in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates.
He said shippers were dissatisfied with service, saying air cargo lacked transparency, had improved little over the past 20 years and was marked by industry in-fighting.

He said studies showed that in 1974, an average international air cargo consignment took six days and six hours to transit from shipper to consignee. In 1995, the average cycle was still six days, he said.
"In 20 years we have taken six hours off the cycle time. would anyone of us here buy a 1974 car if they had the choice?" Doyle said.
He said integrators were doing a much better job than traditional freight at streamlining the cargo process.
Doyle said integrators would increasingly eat into the market share of the traditional freight industry. "And that's not express service, but all time-definite service," he said.
From less than 10 percent of market share in 1995, he said integrators offering time-definite services would account for about 50 percent by 2015.

He said that traditional freight goes through an average of 40 processes per parcel against 11 processes with integrators. Traditional freight services store an average parcel on eight occasions versus zero storage with integrators.
"A fundamental change is coming," Doyle said. "I'm not saying that the traditional industry is the same as integrators. It's a rational world versus an irrational world."
Unisys is an information management company that provides information services technology software and customer service on a worldwide basis.
The two-day cargo conference in Sharjah, which began on Sunday, is hosted by the Sharjah Airport Authority and organised by the Airports Council International, a world organisation for airports.
